content.text:
**Built, tested, committed** (`ac37809`).

## What you now have

A fourth ritual in `ritual-check.ps1` that enforces the Wednesday capture instead of relying on you remembering. It detects captures from the artifact itself — newest `*_baylor.csv` in `data/weekly_snapshots/` — following the script's existing rule that *"a state file can drift from reality, the artifact cannot."*

Verified across every case:

| Simulated date | Result |
|---|---|
| Wed 2026-09-09, no capture | **DUE** |
| Thu 2026-09-10 | **OVERDUE** |
| Season opener Wed 08-26 | **DUE** |
| Today (pre-season) | **OK**, silent |

**The schedule already covers it** — `com.keystone.rituals` fires Mon–Fri 17:00 plus Fri 15:30, giving you Wed DUE → Thu OVERDUE → Fri OVERDUE ×2 before Saturday kickoff. No plist change needed.

## The blocker I found on the way

**`-Notify` has been mute on this Mac since the migration.** It shelled out to `msg.exe` — Windows-only — so every scheduled run since landed in the catch block and wrote "desktop prompt unavailable" into a log nobody reads. The launchd agent has been firing on time, into silence.

That's the exact failure this script was written to prevent, reproduced inside its own alarm. And it explains what you're seeing: **interview-me is 12 days overdue, weekly-review 15** — nothing has been nagging you. Now on `osascript`, dialog with a banner fallback; I fired a live 3-second test and it displayed correctly.

Adding a CFB ritual to a mute alarm would have accomplished nothing, so this was in scope rather than a detour.

## Two deliberate design choices worth your disagreement

Both are cases where the alarm **stays silent and looks broken**:

1. **Sun/Mon/Tue after a missed week → OK.** The window has closed; that forecast is gone. Nagging about something unfixable is how an alarm trains you to ignore it — and this one has to still be believed on the Wednesday that matters.
2. **Outside 8/26–1/20 → OK**, however stale the last capture.

A naive "days since last capture" implementation would scream in both. Tests pin them as the discriminating cases, so a later simplification can't quietly invert the logic.

If you'd rather it nag on Sun/Mon/Tue anyway — as a "you lost a week" postmortem signal rather than an action prompt — that's a one-line change and a reasonable different call.

The CFB weekly forecast freeze had no Mac-side guard. It is the only ritual
protecting a non-backfillable artifact: a pre-game forecast is capturable only
before kickoff, so a missed Wednesday is a permanently absent week in the
series rather than a chore that rolls forward. Season opens 2026-08-26.

The alarm is deliberately silent in two cases that look like bugs:
  - outside the season window (Aug 26 - Jan 20), and
  - Sun/Mon/Tue after a missed week, when the window has already closed and
    no action remains.
Nagging about an unfixable thing is how an alarm teaches you to ignore it, and
this one has to still be believed on the Wednesday that matters. Live window is
Wed (DUE) -> Thu/Fri/Sat (OVERDUE), which the existing launchd schedule already
covers at Wed/Thu/Fri 17:00 plus Fri 15:30.

Also fixes -Notify, which has been mute since the Windows migration: it shelled
out to msg.exe, absent on macOS, so every scheduled run landed in the catch and
wrote 'desktop prompt unavailable' to a log nobody reads. That is precisely the
invisible-absence failure this script exists to prevent, reproduced inside its
own alarm. Now uses osascript, falling back from dialog to notification banner.

Adds -Today and -CfbSnapshotDir seams so the date- and season-dependent logic is
testable; tests/keystone-ritual-forecast-capture.ps1 pins both silent cases,
which a days-since-last-capture implementation would fail.

The report's "Chance of Victory" column is **overwritten with the realised
result** once a game is played. Across 2019–2025 that destroyed every pre-game

gone permanently — it cannot be recovered later. This makes 2026 the first
gradable season.

`Team attempt 1 failed, retrying...` in the output is **normal** — the first
slicer interaction races the app's own start-up. It retries 3×. Only treat it
as a failure if all attempts are exhausted.

Lead with whether the capture succeeded and the game count, then:

input.content:
# tests/keystone-ritual-forecast-capture.ps1
#
# The forecast-capture ritual guards the one NON-BACKFILLABLE artifact in the set.
# cfbvictorymodel.com overwrites its "Chance of Victory" column with the realised
# result once a game is played, so a pre-game probability not captured before
# Saturday's kickoffs is destroyed permanently. 2019-2025 were lost this way.
#
# The alarm shape follows from that, and these tests pin the parts that look wrong:
#
#   1. SILENT outside the season window. A days-based alarm screams through
#      February about a capture nobody can take.
#   2. SILENT on Sunday. Saturday's games have already overwritten the week; there
#      is no action left. Nagging about an unfixable thing is how an alarm teaches
#      you to ignore it, and this one must still be believed on Monday.
#   3. RECHECK, not silence, when the capture happened EARLIER this week and it is
#      still Mon-Wed. An early capture may have grabbed numbers the source had not
#      yet refreshed after the previous weekend; going quiet on it would let a
#      stale snapshot masquerade as a good week. This is the case a naive
#      "captured this week -> OK" implementation gets wrong.
#
# Capture-day escalation is Monday DUE -> Tue-Sat OVERDUE, anchored on Monday so
# the first warning lands early in the week rather than midweek.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
function Assert-True($Condition, $Message) { if (-not $Condition) { throw $Message } }
$repoRoot = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..")
$tempRoot = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("keystone-cfb-test-" + [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("n"))

function New-Fixture {
    param([string[]]$CaptureDates)
    $root  = Join-Path $tempRoot ([System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("n"))
    $vault = Join-Path $root "vault"
    $snaps = Join-Path $root "snapshots"
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $root "scripts"), (Join-Path $root "decisions"),
                                              (Join-Path $vault "output"), (Join-Path $vault "Inbox/weekly-review"),
                                              $snaps | Out-Null
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repoRoot "scripts/ritual-check.ps1") -Destination (Join-Path $root "scripts/ritual-check.ps1")
    Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $root "decisions/log.md") -Value "# Decisions Log`n" -Encoding UTF8
    Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $vault "output/_ledger.md") -Value "| Date | Artifact |`n|---|---|`n" -Encoding UTF8
    # Real capture filenames look like 2026-07-31_baylor.csv - one per team per run.
    foreach ($d in $CaptureDates) {
        Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $snaps "${d}_baylor.csv") -Value "week,opponent`n1,someone`n" -Encoding UTF8
    }
    [pscustomobject]@{ Script = (Join-Path $root "scripts/ritual-check.ps1"); Vault = $vault; Snaps = $snaps }
}

function Get-Cfb {
    param($Fixture, [string]$Today)
    $out = & $Fixture.Script -Json -Vault $Fixture.Vault -CfbSnapshotDir $Fixture.Snaps -Today $Today 2>&1 | Out-String
    ($out | ConvertFrom-Json) | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'forecast-capture' }
}

try {
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')) '2026-09-07'
    Assert-True ($null -ne $c) "forecast-capture must appear in the ritual list."

    # --- not captured: Monday is the nag day, then escalate ------------------
    # Previous week's capture (08-31 Mon) does not satisfy the 09-07 week.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-08-31')) '2026-09-07'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'DUE') "Monday with no capture this week must be DUE, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-08-31')) '2026-09-08'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OVERDUE') "Tuesday with no capture must be OVERDUE, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-08-31')) '2026-09-09'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OVERDUE') "Wednesday with no capture must be OVERDUE, got '$($c.Status)'."
    # Saturday is kickoff day - still the last chance for later games.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-08-31')) '2026-09-12'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OVERDUE') "Saturday with no capture must be OVERDUE, got '$($c.Status)'."

    # Never captured at all, in season, on a Monday.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @()) '2026-09-07'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -ne 'OK') "Never-captured in season must raise a nudge, got '$($c.Status)'."
    Assert-True ($c.Last -eq 'never') "No captures must report Last='never', got '$($c.Last)'."

    # --- captured today satisfies today --------------------------------------
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')) '2026-09-07'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Captured today (Mon) must be OK, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-09')) '2026-09-09'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Captured today (Wed) must be OK, got '$($c.Status)'."

    # --- DISCRIMINATING CASE 1: early capture keeps nagging through Wed ------
    # Captured Monday. The source may not have refreshed after the previous
    # weekend's games yet, so an early snapshot can be stale. Staying quiet would
    # let that stale capture pass for a good week - the failure this guards.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')) '2026-09-08'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'RECHECK') "Captured Mon, checked Tue must be RECHECK, got '$($c.Status)'."
    Assert-True ($c.Why -match 'refresh') "RECHECK Why must explain the refresh risk; got '$($c.Why)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')) '2026-09-09'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'RECHECK') "Captured Mon, checked Wed must be RECHECK, got '$($c.Status)'."
    # Thursday onward the re-check window closes and an existing capture is enough.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')) '2026-09-10'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Captured Mon, checked Thu must be OK, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')) '2026-09-12'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Captured Mon, checked Sat must be OK, got '$($c.Status)'."

    # --- DISCRIMINATING CASE 2: Sunday is silent -----------------------------
    # Saturday's games have overwritten the week. Nothing can be done.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-08-31')) '2026-09-13'
    Assert-True ($c.Days -ge 13) "Fixture must be genuinely stale to discriminate; Days=$($c.Days)."
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Sunday after a missed week must be silent (Days=$($c.Days)), got '$($c.Status)'."

    # --- DISCRIMINATING CASE 3: out of season --------------------------------
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-07-31')) '2026-08-01'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Before the season window must be OK, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2027-01-13')) '2027-02-01'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "After the season window must be OK, got '$($c.Status)'."
    Assert-True ($c.Why -match 'season') "Off-season Why must say so; got '$($c.Why)'."

    # --- season boundaries ----------------------------------------------------
    # The window opens on the MONDAY of the opening week so the first nag lands
    # early, not on the documented Wednesday opener.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @()) '2026-08-24'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'DUE') "Opening Monday must be DUE, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @()) '2026-08-23'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Day before the window opens must be silent, got '$($c.Status)'."
    # ...and closes on the Saturday of the final week, so the last week stays
    # actionable through kickoff rather than going quiet on the Thursday.
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2027-01-11')) '2027-01-23'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OVERDUE') "Closing Saturday must still be OVERDUE, got '$($c.Status)'."
    $c = Get-Cfb (New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2027-01-11')) '2027-01-24'
    Assert-True ($c.Status -eq 'OK') "Day after the window closes must be silent, got '$($c.Status)'."

    # --- the other rituals must survive the new parameters -------------------
    $f = New-Fixture -CaptureDates @('2026-09-07')
    $all = (& $f.Script -Json -Vault $f.Vault -CfbSnapshotDir $f.Snaps -Today '2026-09-07' 2>&1 | Out-String | ConvertFrom-Json)
    Assert-True ($all.Count -eq 4) "Expected 4 rituals, got $($all.Count)."
    foreach ($n in @('interview-me','weekly-review','harvest','forecast-capture')) {
        Assert-True ($all.Name -contains $n) "Ritual '$n' missing from the list."
    }

    Write-Host "keystone forecast-capture ritual tests passed"
}
finally { if (Test-Path $tempRoot) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $tempRoot -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } }

## What changed

Reading the skill corrected my understanding of your constraint. There's no scheduled system update — **the report overwrites "Chance of Victory" with the realised result once a game is *played***. So the wall is Saturday's kickoffs, which makes moving the warning earlier straightforwardly right.

The `RECHECK` status is the protective piece you chose: an early capture isn't proof of a *good* capture, since the source may not have refreshed the coming weekend's numbers on Monday. Going quiet would let a stale snapshot pass for a done week. Capturing today always satisfies today — `RECHECK` means *verify*, not *you missed it*.

I also widened the season bounds to the Monday of the opening week (08-24) and the Saturday of the closing week (01-23), so neither end truncates a live capture window.

**One limitation worth knowing:** `com.keystone.rituals` only fires Mon–Fri. Monday's DUE and the Tue–Fri escalation all land, but **Saturday's OVERDUE is only visible if you run the check by hand** — it's a manual safety net, not a live alarm. Friday 15:30 and 17:00 are your last automated warnings. Say the word if you want a Saturday trigger; the tradeoff is that the other three rituals would then nag you on weekends too.

## On the errors log

Diagnosed, and it's the benign case: a healthy `memsearch index` (94% CPU, genuinely working) held the lock, and the SessionEnd hook's 50 s timeout kept losing the race. The streak counter escalates at 6 and had reached 12.

This is the residual your own note predicts — the shared counter can escalate during a long index even though nothing is broken. I've queued a verification that waits for the lock, confirms a clean index run, and only then clears the counter. I did **not** touch the database.

Worth flagging as a pattern rather than an incident: `ms-search` protects *reads* from this, but hook-driven *writes* still have no lock-aware retry. That's the gap generating these entries. Not fixing it unprompted — but it'll keep recurring during long indexes.

=== morning-cadence.ps1 (what it does) ===
# Runs the KeystoneOS morning packet + dashboard refresh. Called by the
# 'KeystoneOS Morning' scheduled task; safe to run manually.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$keystone = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "keystone.ps1"
$log = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "../outputs/morning/cadence.log"
try {
    & $keystone morning *>> $log
    & $keystone meeting-sync *>> $log
    # Portfolio dashboard daily re-render (project-triage/render.py). Runs
    # before snapshot so the snapshot's Front Burner section reflects today's
    # pulse, not yesterday's. Non-fatal: a render failure here must never
    # break the rest of the morning cadence.
    try {
        & "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/render.py" 2>&1 |
            ForEach-Object { Add-Content $log "[portfolio] $_" }
    } catch {
        Add-Content $log "[portfolio] render failed: $_"
    }
    & $keystone snapshot *>> $log
    & $keystone dashboard *>> $log
    & $keystone cockpit *>> $log
    # Drift guard: cadence keeps the generated layer fresh, but nothing was
    # watching the hand-written layer go stale. Never fails the cadence.
    & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "os-freshness.ps1") *>> $log
    # Ritual guard: a skipped ritual leaves no error, only an absence. Both

for a retired project is its old directory; put the repo URL in a separate field
(`restoreFrom`) that nothing treats as a path.

consumers before trusting the edit — `scripts/keystone.ps1 dashboard`, `cockpit`, `snapshot`

This system is well-instrumented, which makes its few misleading surfaces
dangerous — they look authoritative. Check these before drawing conclusions.

**"Did a job run today?"** Only `KeystoneOS Morning` runs through `run-job.ps1`;
AgySync, DailyBackup, MsysKeepAlive, Reconcile, Rituals and StackDoctor invoke
their scripts directly and write **no ledger row**. So `outputs/run-ledger.json`
under-reports. Correctness is fine — `Test-JobCompleteOn` checks the ledger *or*
the job's `successProbe`. Ask `.\scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun -Json`,
never the ledger alone and never `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo`.

**memsearch timeout streaks are not failures.** The 45s SessionEnd hook is
deliberately best-effort (`daily-backup.ps1:122-125`); the uncapped nightly at
00:30 absorbs backlog and resets the counter. A streak of 16 on 2026-07-28 was
read as a broken indexer and produced a whole plan step to "fix" it — the nightly
cleared it the same night, exactly as designed. Alarm threshold is 6.

**The test suite is main-checkout-only.** `Get-KeystoneDevRoot` resolves the DEV
root as `<repoRoot>\..`, which from a worktree yields
`KeystoneOS\.claude\worktrees\`. `tests\keystone-reconcile.ps1` therefore always
throws in a worktree. Baseline on main is 23 pass / 1 fail
(`skill-verification-contracts.ps1`, unrelated). Always baseline against main
before blaming a change.

**Three claims failed verification in one session (2026-07-28/29):** that the
registry pointed at a stale clone, that the reconciler was wasting hours on
redundant backups, and that the indexer was chronically broken. All three were
plausible from a point-in-time reading and all three were wrong. State a claim

**I broke your morning cadence last night, and the rescan caught it.**

## The regression

When I retired morning-briefing, I set `canonicalPath` in `projects.json` to the GitHub URL — reasoning that pointing at a deleted directory would trip the os-audit. That field is consumed as a real path, and at 06:00 this morning the cadence died at the dashboard step:

```
cadence FAILED: Cannot find drive. A drive with the name 'https' does not exist.
```

I confirmed the mechanism rather than assuming it: `Join-Path`, `Get-Item`, `Resolve-Path`, `Get-ChildItem`, and `Convert-Path` **all throw that exact string** on a URL.

The nasty part — and my first hypothesis was wrong here — is that **`Test-Path` returns `False` on a URL instead of throwing.** That's why the `if (-not (Test-Path $Path))` guards in `Get-PathSummary` and `Get-GitSummary` sail straight past it and the failure surfaces somewhere downstream. A path that merely doesn't exist is handled cleanly; a URL is not.

Fixed in `a27256e`: `canonicalPath` restored to the old directory, URL moved to a new `restoreFrom` field. Verified `dashboard`, `cockpit`, `snapshot`, and `os-freshness` all pass, and a full cadence run is going now to clear the launchd exit code.

The lesson I wrote to memory: **JSON validity proves nothing here** — the file parsed fine and still took down the cadence. Run the consumers after editing any `data/*.json`.

## The CFB work (unaffected)

Committed `5bc1503`. Monday-anchored, verified across a full simulated week:

- Never captured: **Mon DUE → Tue–Sat OVERDUE → Sun silent**
- Captured Monday: **Mon OK → Tue/Wed RECHECK → Thu+ OK**

`RECHECK` is the protection you asked for — an early capture may have grabbed numbers the source hadn't refreshed yet, so it keeps surfacing through Wednesday instead of going quiet.

## Also cleared

The `memsearch` ETIMEDOUT streak was benign — a healthy index (94% CPU) holding the lock while the hook's 50 s timeout kept losing the race. Verified a clean index run, reset the counter (was 13), and `.errors.log` is empty. Index at 10,131 chunks with retrieval confirmed working.
